name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index 103.4 on 16 Nov, a 52-week high, up 4.6% over three months; just inside the 5% Watch line
state: The DXY dollar index was near 103.4 early on 16 Nov, its highest in a year, up 4.6% over three months and 1.1% on the week (Yahoo Finance). That is just inside the 5% three-month Watch line and well within the 90–108 range. SOFR equalled the Fed's reserve rate on 12 Nov, showing no dollar funding strain (FRED).
for_you: A stronger dollar makes dollar-priced goods, including fuel, dearer for UK and European buyers and raises costs for dollar borrowers abroad.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 4.81% below the 5% Watch line
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
